x: Group O red cells carry no A or B antigen, so O (strictly O negative) is the universal donor; AB is the universal recipient.
The liver is the largest gland of the human body; the pancreas is second. The spleen is not a gland and the pituitary is pea-sized.
When the kidneys fail, blood is cleaned artificially by dialysis (haemodialysis or peritoneal). Radiolysis, pyrolysis and hydrolysis are chemical breakdown processes, not treatments.
Man-made chemicals that interfere with the hormone system (BPA, phthalates, some pesticides) are called endocrine disruptors. 'Facilitators', 'reactors' and 'inhibitors' are not the accepted term.
evidence: NIEHS, Endocrine Disruptors (niehs.nih.gov/health/topics/agents/endocrine): natural or man-made chemicals that mimic, block or interfere with hormones

x: Artificial muscles have been developed to help a failing heart pump (e.g. a soft robotic sleeve around the heart), so heart is keyed; the source news item behind this question was not traced.
source: printed key, not verified (artificial-muscle news items: heart-assist soft robotic sleeve; skeletal-muscle implants also reported)
evidence: Web search: artificial muscle reports cover heart-assist devices (Harvard soft robotic sleeve, 2017) and skeletal-muscle implants (Natl Sci Rev 2024); no single source for the question found

x: A pacemaker is a device that regulates the heartbeat (the heart's own pacemaker is the SA node), so it is related to the heart.
Blood group AB has both A and B antigens and no anti-A or anti-B antibodies, so it is the universal recipient; O negative is the universal donor.
The pancreas is both endocrine (insulin from Islets of Langerhans) and exocrine (digestive enzymes). Liver, testis and pituitary are not described this way.
The adrenal glands sit above the kidneys, so the adrenal gland is the one on the kidney. The pituitary, thyroid and hypothalamus are in the brain or neck.

Glucagon raises blood glucose through glycogenolysis, gluconeogenesis from amino acids, and reduced hepatic glucose uptake; the statement about cell growth, immunity, fetal development and vision describes vitamin A, not glucagon.
The adrenal glands sit above the kidneys, so the adrenal gland is the one on the kidney. The pituitary, thyroid and hypothalamus are in the brain or neck.
The lacrimal gland secretes tear fluid that is spread over the eye by blinking. The thyroid, salivary and pituitary glands have no such role.
source: NCERT Class X Science; lacrimal gland, general physiology

x: Insulin promotes glucose uptake and fat storage and lowers blood sugar, including by slowing glycogen breakdown in the liver, so all of the listed functions are correct.
In diabetes mellitus the pancreas produces insufficient insulin (or cells resist it), so glucose accumulates in the blood.
The liver is the largest gland in the human body, performing vital functions such as detoxification, protein synthesis, bile production and metabolism regulation.
The liver is renowned for its regenerative capacity, restoring a large proportion of lost mass and function within a few weeks after partial removal.
The hormonal output from the thyroid is regulated by thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) produced by the anterior pituitary.
The normal average blood pressure of human is 120/80 mm Hg. This means that systolic pressure around 120mm Hg and diastolic pressure should be around 80 mm Hg.
Normal human body temperature is about 37°C (98.6°F). 98°C is far too high; 367 K is about 94°C, not 37°C (310 K).
source: NCERT Class VII Science ch.4 (normal body temperature 37 °C)

x: Thalassemia is a genetic blood disorder. In a patient of Thalassemia, the body is unable to synthesise enough haemoglobin, which causes severe anaemia.
Dialysis removes waste and excess water from the blood and replaces lost kidney function. Haemolysis is RBC breakdown and osmosis is water movement across a membrane.
The eye's lens focuses light to form the image on the retina, which holds the photoreceptors. The cornea, iris and pupil do not form the image.
Plucking a sitar string sets up a transverse wave that reflects from the fixed ends, forming a stationary (standing) transverse wave.
Thyroxine (T4) and T3 from the thyroid contain iodine (T4 has four iodine atoms). Insulin, adrenaline and testosterone contain no iodine.
The kidneys remove urea and other nitrogenous wastes from the blood, so when they fail these wastes accumulate. Fats, proteins and sugar are not what builds up.
Vitamin A is largely stored in the liver in the human body. Its chemical name is retinol whose deficiency causes night blindness.

Blood group A individuals have the A antigen on the surface of their RBCs and blood serum containing IgM antibodies against the B antigen. Therefore, group A individual can receive blood only from individuals of groups A or O (with A being preferable) and can donate blood to individuals with type A or AB.

The treatment options for kidney failure are peritoneal dialysis (PD), hemodialysis and kidney transplant. A dialyzer is an artificial kidney designed to provide controllable transfer of solutes and water across a semipermeable membrane separating flowing blood and dialysate streams.
ATP → ADP + Pi releases the energy cells use (ATP is the energy currency). ADP → ATP stores energy rather than providing it.
Darkness raises melatonin and bright light suppresses it, so A is true (light disturbs sleep) but R is false.
Insulin is secreted by the beta cells of the Islets of Langerhans in the pancreas, not by the pituitary, thyroid or adrenal glands.

Parathyroid hormone is controlled by blood calcium, not by a pituitary tropic hormone, so the parathyroid works independently. Thyroid (TSH), adrenal cortex (ACTH) and gonads (FSH/LH) depend on the pituitary.
Estrone is a weak postmenopausal estrogen and a minor female sex hormone. Estrogen (Oestrogen) is the actual female sex hormone.
source: NCERT Class XI Biology ch.22 (estrogens = female sex hormones)

x: Vitamin A is a fat-soluble vitamin that is stored in the liver, so the liver is the correct answer.
In humans, kidneys are the main organ of the excretion system. Filtering the blood and removing unnecessary and waste products from the body is the basic function of kidney.
Parathyroid hormone (PTH) raises blood calcium and increases phosphate excretion, so it regulates both. Glucagon controls sugar; growth hormone and thyroxine do not mainly regulate calcium.
Iodised salt is table salt mixed with a minute amount of various salts of the element iodine. Iodine deficiency can cause thyroid gland problems.

The process, ultrafiltration occurs at the barrier between the blood and the filtrate in the renal capsule in the kidney. The kidneys remove urea and other toxic wastes from the blood, forming a dilute solution called urine in the process.
Oxytocin is made in the hypothalamus and released by the posterior pituitary, so the pituitary is keyed. Thyroid, parathyroid and adrenal glands do not secrete it.
Most compilations key the kidney as the organ most affected by long fasting. The question is loose (see the dispute line), but kidney is the commonly taught answer.
source: printed key, not verified (commonly keyed answer in SSC/UPPSC compilations)
evidence: NextGen Rocket Biology: no fasting fact
dispute: Most books and keys: kidney. Strictly: the question is loose – prolonged fasting first drains liver glycogen and then muscle protein; the kidney is stressed by ketones and dehydration.

x: The cornea and lens focus light so that the image forms on the retina, which sends it to the brain through the optic nerve.

In urine, there are about 91-96% water, about 2% unuseful salt ions, about 2.6% urea, about 0.3% creatinine and very small amount of uric acid and some other useless matter. The presence of albumin (a protein found in blood plasma) in it increases the chance of kidney failure.
Adrenaline from the adrenal medulla prepares the body for 'fight or flight' – faster heartbeat, more blood to muscles. Insulin, estrogen and oxytocin have no such role.
Bright's disease is inflammation of the kidneys (nephritis) with albumin in the urine. It does not affect the spleen, heart or liver.
source: NCERT Class XI Biology ch.19; Britannica 'Bright disease' (nephritis)

x: An adult skeleton has 206 bones, so about 200 at age 20. A newborn has about 300, which is why that option tempts.
The liver converts toxic ammonia into urea. Lipase comes from the pancreas, HCl from the stomach and mucus from many linings.
Haemoglobin is red and carries oxygen to the cells and some CO2 back to the lungs, so 'slightly acidic' is the statement keyed as not correct.
evidence: Haemoglobin isoelectric point ~pH 6.8 (chl.co.nz Hb electrophoresis note)
dispute: Most books and keys: 'slightly acidic' is the wrong statement. Strictly: haemoglobin behaves as a weak acid (isoelectric pH ~6.8, so it is anionic at blood pH 7.4), so the statement is arguable; the other three are plainly true.

x: Connective tissues include bone, cartilage and blood. Skeletal muscle is muscular tissue, not connective tissue.
Tendons connect muscle to bone. Ligaments connect bone to bone; neurons and adipose tissue do not join muscles to bones.
A reflex action is coordinated by the spinal cord, so the response occurs without waiting for the brain. The cerebrum handles voluntary action.
White blood cells such as neutrophils defend the body against infection. Red cells carry oxygen and platelets help clotting.
An adult human skeleton has 206 bones. 200 is only an approximation, so 206 is the exact answer.
The ear ossicles are the malleus, incus and stapes. The femur is the thigh bone in the leg, not part of the ear.
The normal resting heart rate of a healthy adult is about 72 beats per minute.
Light enters through the pupil and then passes through the lens, so the lens lies just behind the pupil. The retina is at the back of the eye.
Needing glasses only to read a newspaper is the typical sign of presbyopia, the age-related loss of accommodation corrected with convex (reading) lenses. Myopia blurs distant objects.
evidence: NextGen Rocket Physics p.71 (hypermetropia: nearby objects blurred; presbyopia: age-related loss of accommodation)
byjus.com question page keys presbyopia; testbook.com keys hypermetropia
dispute: Most books and keys: presbyopia. Some keys give hypermetropia, which also blurs near objects; presbyopia (age-related loss of accommodation) is the usual reason a person needs glasses only to read.

x: Ear muscles are vestigial in humans: they are reduced and functionless, though they are functional in other animals. Jaw, canine teeth and humerus are functional.
The retina is the light-sensitive surface on which the image forms, like the film in a camera. The lens of the eye corresponds to the camera lens.
Mother O has genotype OO, and father A may be AO. The child can be A or O.
The epididymis, vas deferens, seminal vesicles and prostate are accessory ducts and glands. They mature and carry sperms and provide fluid for motility.
source: NCERT Class XII Biology ch.3 (male accessory ducts and glands)

x: Active immunity arises when the body's own cells make antibodies after infection or vaccination, so statement I is correct. Anti-venom gives ready-made antibodies, which is passive immunisation, so statement II is wrong.
NCERT lists short stature, a furrowed tongue and mental retardation for Down's syndrome (trisomy 21), but not early ageing, so option 2 is the statement keyed as not correct.
Tubectomy is the surgical cutting and ligation of the fallopian tube (oviduct) in females. Vasectomy is the male procedure on the vas deferens.
The eustachian tube connects the middle ear to the pharynx and equalises air pressure on both sides of the eardrum. Malleus and incus are ossicles that transmit vibrations.
Colostrum is the first milk after childbirth. It is rich in antibodies and builds the newborn's immunity.
source: NCERT Class XII Biology ch.8 (colostrum, passive immunity)

x: In common red–green colour blindness red and green are confused, so red appears greenish; it is not seen as yellow, blue or violet.
Myoglobin is an iron-containing oxygen-storing protein in muscle. Chlorophyll contains magnesium, while collagen and carotene contain no iron.
Oxygen enters the lungs first, is carried by the blood, and is then delivered to the tissues: lungs, blood, tissue.
Only the coronary artery statement is correct. The pulmonary vein carries blood from the lungs to the heart, the renal artery supplies the kidneys, and the hepatic artery supplies the liver.
Water is reabsorbed in the renal tubules and the large intestine. Hepatic cells and the pancreatic duct do not absorb water.

Somatotropin (growth hormone) rises with exercise, the testes make small amounts of progesterone, and the female adrenal secretes some testosterone, so I, II and III are correct. Stress raises cortisol, so IV is wrong.
Glaucoma damages the optic nerve and worsens progressively, usually due to raised eye pressure. Cataract affects the lens.
source: NCERT Class X Science ch.10; AIIMS/NEI: glaucoma = optic-nerve damage

x: Respiration changes the O2 (21% to 16%) and CO2 (0.04% to 4%) content of air, while nitrogen is not used and stays unchanged.
source: NCERT Class X Science ch.6 (inhaled vs exhaled air)

x: Haemoglobin in RBCs carries mainly oxygen, and also some carbon dioxide (as carbamino-haemoglobin). It is not for clotting.
Insulin is secreted by the beta cells of the pancreas; alpha cells secrete glucagon.
Bones consist mainly of calcium phosphate (hydroxyapatite), so it is the salt found in maximum amount.
A mid-cycle surge of luteinizing hormone triggers ovulation.
The ovary is the primary sex organ in females since it produces ova and hormones. The uterus, vagina and fallopian tube are accessory organs.
The cervix is part of the female reproductive system (the neck of the uterus). The urethra, seminal vesicle and vas deferens are in the male system.
A male child is XY. The Y chromosome can only come from the father and the X from the mother.
source: NCERT Class X Science ch.8 (sex determination)

x: The oesophagus is the food pipe carrying food from the pharynx to the stomach. The larynx is the voice box, the aorta is an artery and the thymus is a gland.
Saliva contains salivary amylase, which begins the digestion of starch in the mouth.
Urine is yellow due to the pigment urochrome, formed from the breakdown of haemoglobin.
The corpus luteum forms in the ovary from the ruptured follicle after ovulation and secretes progesterone.
Tendons are made of collagen, a tough fibrous protein. Fibrin is for clotting, elastin is in elastic tissue and cellulose is not a protein.
Thrombin is the enzyme that converts fibrinogen into fibrin during blood clotting; it has no role in excretion, reproduction or growth.
Group B donates to B and AB. AB is the universal recipient, so B can donate to AB.
Oxygenated blood returns from the lungs through the pulmonary veins to the left auricle (atrium), then passes to the left ventricle.
Haemophilia is an X-linked disorder in which a clotting factor is missing, so the blood does not clot. It does not lower haemoglobin or WBC count.
Wilson's disease is copper accumulation, causing neurological symptoms, liver problems and fluid build-up. Night blindness is caused by vitamin A deficiency, so it is not a symptom.
Haemophilia A is the X-linked recessive disorder caused by a deficiency of clotting factor VIII. The others are blood cancers or a clotting disorder (thrombosis), not factor VIII deficiency.
The ciliary muscles of the ciliary body change the curvature of the lens and so its focal length (accommodation). The retina only receives the image.
Bile is made in the liver but stored and concentrated in the gall bladder, which is why 'liver' is the tempting wrong option.
Lymphocytes form from stem cells in the red bone marrow of (long) bones; the spleen and lymph nodes store and activate them but are not where they are formed.
The thick-walled left ventricle pumps fully oxygenated blood into the aorta for the whole body. The right ventricle sends deoxygenated blood to the lungs.
AB is the universal recipient, so A can donate to AB. A cannot donate to O, B cannot donate to A, and AB cannot donate to O.
Urine is made in the kidneys, flows down the ureters to the bladder and leaves through the urethra.
Of the listed glands the pea-sized pituitary is the smallest; the liver is the largest gland and the thyroid the largest endocrine gland.
The pituitary is the master gland and controls other endocrine glands through hormones such as TSH and ACTH.
The thymus lies behind the sternum, between the lungs, and trains T cells. The pituitary and pineal glands are in the brain.
Cortisol is a steroid hormone from the adrenal gland, so it has no peptide chain. Oxytocin, corticotropin (ACTH) and insulin are peptide hormones.
Thyroxine (T4) from the thyroid regulates the metabolic rate. Blood glucose is controlled by insulin, not thyroxine.
Cretinism in children results from under-secretion of thyroxine by the thyroid. Adrenaline and cortisone are adrenal hormones and glycogen is not a hormone.
The adrenal gland is called the life-saving gland because adrenaline and cortisol help the body survive stress and emergencies.
Adrenaline from the adrenal gland is the emergency hormone, used in fight-or-flight situations.
Gastrin is a hormone secreted by the stomach lining, not a gland. Thyroid, liver (the largest gland) and pancreas are all glands.
Insulin is secreted by the beta cells of the Islets of Langerhans in the pancreas, so pancreas is correct.
Insulin comes from the Islets of Langerhans (beta cells) of the pancreas, not the spleen, gonads or liver.
The adrenal glands secrete adrenaline and cortisol, which regulate blood pressure; parathyroid, thyroid and thymus do not primarily do so.
The pituitary is a single gland at the base of the brain, while the adrenals, testes and ovaries occur in pairs.
In diabetes mellitus blood glucose is high and excess glucose is excreted in urine, carrying water with it, so the person drinks more water to eliminate glucose.
Sodium ions (Na+), with potassium, create the ion movements across nerve cell membranes that carry electrical signals. Lithium, rubidium and caesium are not needed for this.
Neurons are specialised for excitability (responding to stimuli) and conductivity (transmitting impulses). Elasticity and flexibility are not their properties.
Hypermetropia is corrected by a convex (converging) lens, while concave lenses correct myopia.
The eye lens acts like a convex lens in a camera and forms a real, inverted image on the retina, which the brain interprets as upright.
Human blood is slightly basic, about pH 7.4; the only basic range offered, 7.5-8.0, is keyed. Ranges below 7 would be acidic and 8.5-9.0 is far too basic.
source: NextGen Rocket Chemistry (src/science-tech/rocket-chemistry.txt) p.21 (blood pH 7.4, slightly basic)
evidence: NextGen Rocket Chemistry p.21: blood pH 7.4, slightly basic
dispute: Official key / most books: 7.5-8.0 (the only basic range offered). Strictly: normal blood pH is 7.35-7.45, about 7.4 (NextGen Rocket Chemistry p.21).

x: The cerebrum is the seat of memory, thinking and intelligence. The medulla and cerebellum control involuntary functions and balance.
Tachycardia means an abnormally fast heart rate (above normal), whereas a slow rate is bradycardia.
The brain handles thinking (cerebrum), heartbeat regulation (medulla) and body balance (cerebellum), so all of the above is correct.
The pinna is the external part of the ear, not of the brain. Medulla, thalamus and pons are brain parts.
The cerebrum is the largest part of the human brain, much larger than the cerebellum and medulla oblongata.
The eye lens forms images on the retina about 2.5 cm behind it, so the focal length of a normal eye is about 2.5 cm.

The ciliary muscles change the curvature of the eye lens, which alters its focal length (accommodation). The pupil and iris control only the amount of light entering, and the retina receives the image.
Smooth (involuntary) muscle is found in the walls of internal organs like the stomach. Leg and arm muscles are skeletal, and the heart has cardiac muscle.
Human sperms remain viable and capable of fertilising in the female genital tract for about one to two days.
source: NCERT Class XII Biology ch.3 (sperm viability in female tract)

x: The forebrain (cerebrum) is the seat of thinking, intelligence and memory, whereas the midbrain and hindbrain handle reflexes and coordination.
Leydig (interstitial) cells of the testes secrete androgens such as testosterone, while Sertoli cells nourish the developing sperms.
The common bile duct and the pancreatic duct both open into the duodenum, not the stomach, so only statement II is correct.
The human neck has 7 cervical vertebrae, the same number as in most mammals.
Digestion starts in the buccal cavity, where salivary amylase begins breaking down starch. Protein digestion starts in the stomach, which is the tempting wrong option.
The appendix is a vestigial organ with no significant function in humans. The heart, kidney and lungs are vital functioning organs.
Muscle contraction is triggered by Ca2+ released from the sarcoplasmic reticulum, and relaxation occurs when Ca2+ is pumped back into it. It does not depend on Ca2+ from the blood or on Zn.
source: NCERT Class XI Biology ch.20 (sliding filament theory, Ca2+ from sarcoplasmic reticulum)

x: Tooth enamel is mainly calcium phosphate in the form of hydroxyapatite, the hardest substance in the body.
The gastric juice contains hydrochloric acid, secreted by the parietal (oxyntic) cells; it activates pepsinogen to pepsin.
The gastric juice contains hydrochloric acid, secreted by the parietal (oxyntic) cells; it activates pepsinogen to pepsin.
Narrower vessels increase resistance to blood flow, so blood pressure rises.
The kidneys filter urea and other nitrogenous wastes out of the blood, so when they fail these wastes accumulate in the blood. This is why dialysis is needed.
The commonest colour blindness is red-green, caused by a defect in the cone cells that detect red or green light.
The commonest colour blindness is red-green, caused by a defect in the cone cells that detect red or green light.
Food first meets salivary amylase in the mouth, which begins starch digestion. Pepsin acts in the stomach and trypsin in the intestine, so both come later.
Blood, bone and cartilage are connective tissues. Skin is an organ made of epithelial and other tissues, not a connective tissue.
Muscle tissue contains the contractile proteins actin and myosin, which produce contraction.
During sudden strenuous activity muscles respire anaerobically and lactic acid builds up, causing cramps.
Sweat is mostly water with dissolved salts (NaCl) and a little urea. Its salt content makes it taste salty.
source: NCERT Class VII Science (sweat: water and salts)

x: All blood cells, including neutrophils and lymphocytes, originate from stem cells in the bone marrow. Lymph nodes and the spleen only store or mature lymphocytes.

The hepatic portal vein carries nutrient-rich blood from the stomach and small intestine to the liver. The hepatic veins carry blood away from the liver and the hepatic arteries bring it oxygenated blood.
Red blood cells are made in the red bone marrow. The lungs, heart and brain do not make blood cells.
Malpighian tubules are the excretory organs of insects, and the kidneys do the same job in humans by filtering waste such as urea from the blood.
The cerebrum is the largest part of the brain and controls thinking, memory and voluntary action. It is not part of the liver, heart or arteries.
The larynx, nose and external ear have cartilage in their walls. The urinary bladder is a muscular organ with no cartilage.
